description: `new <name> --path <dir> --dry-run` prints plan step 4 as `start '<name>' (already registered)` and stops there — no step 5 (`register` + `start`) — when `<dir>` is already the configured path of a project named `<name>` (new.rs:146-147: `if already_registered { println!("4. start '{name}' (already registered)") } else { ... "4. register..." / "5. start..." }`). The companion `new-dry-run-prints-plan` scenario covers the unregistered branch (steps 4+5); this one is the already-registered branch the Scout finding flagged as untested. Exact `stdout` match (not `_contains`) so a stray step-5 line would fail this. Empty transcript: dry-run returns before any Herdr call.

expect.stdout:
Plan for new project 'already' at <PROJECT:already>:
1. mkdir -p <PROJECT:already> (if it does not already exist)
2. git init -q -b main (if not already a repository)
3. write .gitignore and commit it (if there are no commits yet)
4. start 'already' (already registered)
